_metadata.independence: I read only u14-blind-input.json and no other file, search result, or web source before scoring.

hints.reason: A tiara is a small crown (near-synonym of CROWN) and the classic headpiece a queen or princess wears.
The crown is the royal symbol and the queen is the royal person; broad but reaches both cleanly.
A coronation is literally the crowning ceremony, and the queen is the person crowned in it; one shared scene.

best_available.why: A single ceremony in which a crown is placed on a queen; both words are central to the scene.

pairs.pair_note: Easy pair; all three hints pass. TIARA is a near-synonym of CROWN but still fair.

hints.reason: Gold crown and gold ring are both canonical objects; the shared material is the defining one for both.
Crown Jewels is a familiar compound and a jewel is the stone set in a ring.

best_available.why: Crown Jewels plus the jewel in a ring; both routes are immediate.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; GOLD is a material route but an unusually strong one for two pieces of regalia/jewellery.

hints.reason: Robots are the archetypal metal thing; a crown is a metal (gold) object and 'metal crown' is also the dental term, so the material reaches both.

best_available.why: Only hint; defining for ROBOT and a fair material route for CROWN.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: passed on the shared-property rule (like SWEET for APPLE+HONEY) but the CROWN side is a secondary property.

hints.reason: Crown Jewels for CROWN; a jewel is a precious stone and 'rock' is everyday slang for one ('look at that rock').

best_available.why: Crown Jewels is immediate; jewel-as-rock is a familiar slang step.

pairs.pair_note: Passes, but the ROCK side depends on the player reading rock as gemstone rather than stone or music.

hints.reason: The Tudor rose is a famous emblem and the Tudors are a royal dynasty (the Tudor Crown is also a heraldic symbol).
Crown of thorns is a universally known phrase and roses have thorns.
A garland of roses is a standard phrase and a garland worn on the head is a flower crown/wreath.

best_available.why: Crown of thorns and rose thorns; both routes are instant and broad.

pairs.pair_note: THORN is excellent; TUDOR is good but history-dependent; GARLAND is the softest pass.

hints.reason: Salt tax is a well-known historical compound (gabelle, Salt March); taxes are paid to the Crown, but TAX does not point at CROWN clearly.
Gandhi's Salt March reaches SALT; the march was against the British Crown's monopoly, but a player would not move from GANDHI to CROWN without that explanation.
Both sides are two-step: navy to Royal Navy to Crown, navy to sailor ('old salt') or seawater to SALT; neither reaches clearly.

best_available.why: Salt tax is a real compound and the Crown is the historical tax collector; the most concrete of three stretches.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The pair is hard; all hints lean on the British-Crown-vs-salt-tax story, which only one side of each hint supports.

hints.reason: Heir to the crown is immediate; there is no ordinary route from HEIR to SHADOW.
Crown of the head / crown worn on the head is fine; HEAD gives no recognizable route to SHADOW.
The crown of a tree is a real but moderately known term; trees cast shadows, though 'shade' is the more natural word.

best_available.why: The only hint that touches both words (tree crown; tree shadow), even if each touch is light.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. HEIR and HEAD are pure CROWN filler; TREE is the only two-sided attempt.

hints.reason: Shark teeth are the animal's signature; a dental crown caps a tooth and the crown is the visible part of a tooth.

best_available.why: Both routes are familiar and the dental sense of CROWN is a satisfying twist.

pairs.pair_note: Strong single hint.

hints.reason: The pharaoh's crown carries the cobra (uraeus) and Egypt is linked to snakes via that image and Cleopatra's asp; one shared picture.
Cobra is a kind of snake (hyponym); the CROWN side relies on the cobra on the pharaoh's crown or 'king cobra' to king to crown, both second-step.
A cobra's hood reaches SNAKE via one step; HOOD has no recognizable route to CROWN beyond 'both are on the head'.

best_available.why: The pharaoh's cobra crown binds both words in a single well-known image.

pairs.pair_note: EGYPT is the one two-sided hint; COBRA is a snake hyponym with a thin crown step; HOOD fails.

hints.reason: Crown Jewels is immediate; the 'jewel spider' is an obscure species name and gives no recognizable route to SPIDER.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; it is CROWN-only filler and should not be served.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The pair has no usable hint here.

hints.reason: May is a spring month; the crowning of a May Queen at May Day is a real spring scene but not one most players will reach from MAY alone.
Tree crown is a real term; trees blossom in spring, but TREE points at every season and at many other words first.
Flower crown is a familiar compound and spring flowers are the season's signature.

best_available.why: Flower crown plus spring flowers; both routes are immediate.

pairs.pair_note: FLOWER carries the pair; MAY and TREE are soft.

hints.reason: Stars shine by definition; a crown is shiny, but shining is not a defining property of CROWN the way sweetness is of an apple.

best_available.why: Only hint; shared-property route that is strong for STAR and secondary for CROWN.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Borderline shared-property hint.

hints.reason: Royal crown is immediate; TRAIN is reached via the Royal Train or a royal gown's train, both secondary readings of TRAIN.
Coronation is the crowning; the long train of the coronation robe carried by attendants is an iconic image, so TRAIN (gown sense) is a fair wordplay step.

best_available.why: Crowning scene plus the famous robe train; the most specific route to both words.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: TRAIN is only reached through its garment sense; CORONATION makes that sense concrete, ROYAL does not.

hints.reason: A cap is headwear akin to a crown and 'crown cap' is the bottle-cap term; the cap of a water bottle reaches WATER, but both sides are one step removed.

best_available.why: Only hint; bottle cap touches both (crown cap / water bottle cap) but neither word is immediate.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Clever but indirect.

hints.reason: A queen wears the crown; Snow White's Evil Queen is a witch (and Narnia's White Witch is a queen), a familiar story route like POISON for APPLE+QUEEN.

best_available.why: Crown is immediate and the queen-who-is-a-witch is a well-known fairy-tale figure.

pairs.pair_note: Passes on the Snow White calibration anchor.

hints.reason: Alpha wolf is a familiar compound; the CROWN side is only the metaphor alpha = leader = the one who wears the crown.

best_available.why: Only hint; strong for WOLF, metaphorical for CROWN.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Leader-to-crown is a defensible metaphor but not a clear route.

hints.reason: Dog collar is immediate; a diamond collar (necklace, or the pampered pet's diamond-studded collar) is a recognizable image that joins the two.

best_available.why: One object, a diamond dog collar, contains both words.

pairs.pair_note: Passes; DIAMOND side is secondary but the shared object is familiar.

hints.reason: A dragon's hoard is the classic story image and that hoard is gold and gems, diamonds included.

best_available.why: The dragon-on-its-treasure scene points at both words.

pairs.pair_note: Good single hint.

hints.reason: Faberge egg is a famous compound and Faberge is a jeweller whose eggs are encrusted with diamonds.

best_available.why: The jewelled egg is one object carrying both words.

pairs.pair_note: Passes; players must know Faberge as a jeweller, which most who know the eggs do.

hints.reason: Fire is heat; diamonds famously form under extreme heat and pressure, a widely known fact.
Diamond is pure carbon; fire reaches carbon through charcoal, soot and carbon dioxide, a second step.
Volcanoes are fire and lava; diamonds reach the surface in volcanic kimberlite, a fact fewer players hold.

best_available.why: Heat-and-pressure diamond formation is common knowledge and heat is fire's essence.

pairs.pair_note: HEAT passes; CARBON and VOLCANO are true but each needs a step on one side.

hints.reason: Fish scales are immediate; diamonds are weighed on a jeweller's scales (carats), a plausible but not instant second sense.

best_available.why: Only hint; double meaning touches both but the DIAMOND side is secondary.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Reasonable wordplay, borderline reach.

hints.reason: A diamond is a crystal and crystal is fine glassware; the word also names the diamond imitation.
Diamond cut and cut glass are both standard compounds, and a diamond cuts glass.

best_available.why: Compound on both sides plus the shared scene of a diamond scoring glass.

pairs.pair_note: Both excellent.

hints.reason: Diamond mine and gold mine are both everyday compounds.
Diamond ring and gold ring; a single ring is often both.
Both are the two archetypal jewelry materials; broad but fully two-sided.

best_available.why: One object made of gold and set with a diamond.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass; this pair is naturally close.

hints.reason: Diamond ring is immediate; the ring reaches HEART only through romance or heart-shaped settings.
Diamonds and hearts are two of the four card suits.
Hearts are red and diamonds are the other red suit in a deck; the colour is a defining shared property here, not mood filler.

best_available.why: Both words are card suits; the most direct shared category.

pairs.pair_note: CARD and RED both pass via the deck; RING is one-sided toward DIAMOND.

hints.reason: Clarity is one of the diamond 4 Cs; honey is sold as 'clear' but 'clarity' gives no recognizable route to HONEY.
Diamond is a crystal and honey crystallises in the jar, a familiar kitchen fact.
Raw honey is a shelf label and a raw (uncut) diamond is a recognised phrase even if 'rough' is the trade word.

best_available.why: Direct for the gem and a familiar property of honey.

pairs.pair_note: CRYSTAL and RAW pass; CLARITY is diamond-only.

hints.reason: Diamond stud earrings and a stud horse/stud farm; both senses are everyday.
Horses eat carrots; DIAMOND is reached only through the carrot/carat homophone joke, which is not one of the sanctioned routes.
Diamond ring is immediate; horses are shown in a show ring or circus ring, a secondary sense of RING.

best_available.why: Clean double meaning, both senses broad.

pairs.pair_note: STUD is excellent; CARROT is a pun the rubric does not explicitly allow (flag for owner); RING is soft on HORSE.

hints.reason: Diamonds sparkle by reputation and frost/ice sparkles; 'ice' is also slang for diamonds, so the shared property is a natural bridge.

best_available.why: The property that makes ice a nickname for diamonds.

pairs.pair_note: Passes; the pair is already linked by slang.

hints.reason: Diamond cut is standard; 'cut iron' is not a phrase and IRON is reached only through cast/wrought iron confusion.
Diamond is the hardest material and 'hard as iron' is idiom; the shared property defines both.
Diamond mine and iron (ore) mine are both ordinary compounds.

best_available.why: Concrete compound on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: MINE and HARD pass; CUT is diamond-only.

hints.reason: Diamonds are what you lock in a safe and a key opens the safe; one shared scene.
Diamond cut and 'get a key cut' are both standard usages.

best_available.why: Standard verb/compound on both sides with no story needed.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; SAFE is the more pictorial, CUT the more direct.

hints.reason: The king of diamonds is a playing card; suit and rank both reached.

best_available.why: One card names both words.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: Knight in shining armour is a fixed phrase and 'shine bright like a diamond' / shining diamonds is a familiar property.

best_available.why: Fixed phrase for KNIGHT, defining property for DIAMOND.

pairs.pair_note: Passes.

hints.reason: Diamonds sparkle and sparkle is itself an effect of light.
A prism splits light; a cut diamond's facets act as prisms, giving its rainbow 'fire'.
Diamond cut is standard; CUT has no ordinary route to LIGHT.

best_available.why: Immediate for both words.

pairs.pair_note: SPARKLE and PRISM pass; CUT is diamond-only.

hints.reason: Rock is slang for a diamond; LION is reached only via Pride Rock in The Lion King or lions on a rock, a scene most players will not jump to from ROCK alone.

best_available.why: Only hint; strong for DIAMOND, story-dependent for LION.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: The moon is in the sky; 'like a diamond in the sky' (Twinkle Twinkle) and 'Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds' are both famous.
Diamond ring is immediate; MOON needs the ring/halo around the moon or the eclipse 'diamond ring effect', both secondary.
Rock is slang for a diamond and moon rock is a familiar compound.

best_available.why: Slang for the gem plus the moon rock compound.

pairs.pair_note: ROCK and SKY pass; RING is diamond-leaning.

hints.reason: A mouse is the archetypal tiny animal; diamonds are small but TINY is not a defining property of a diamond.

best_available.why: Only hint; shared size property that is strong for MOUSE and weak for DIAMOND.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: Night sky is a compound; 'like a diamond in the sky' is the famous nursery-rhyme line.
Twinkle Twinkle Little Star compares the star to a diamond and stars twinkle at night; one shared rhyme reaches both.

best_available.why: Night sky compound plus the diamond-in-the-sky line.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass via the nursery rhyme; TWINKLE is the softer of the two.

hints.reason: The ship sank in the ocean and the film's Heart of the Ocean diamond is its central object.

best_available.why: One famous story holds both words.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: Pirate treasure is the compound and diamonds are what treasure chests hold.

best_available.why: Pirate chest full of gems.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: The queen wears the crown and the crown jewels are set with famous diamonds.
The queen of diamonds is a playing card.

best_available.why: One card names both words.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass.

hints.reason: Wedding ring is the compound and the wedding diamond is part of the same scene.
Engagement ring is the compound and the diamond engagement ring is the canonical object.

best_available.why: The diamond engagement ring is the single most familiar object joining both words.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; nearly interchangeable.
